title: [v0.4.29] Tests: verify platform conformance and support
author: mcpdev80
body:
Parent: #818

## Goal

Create the reusable conformance suite, CI matrix and support/evidence rules that prevent platform claims from drifting away from what BaseHarbor actually tests.

## Conformance matrix

At minimum cover:

| Semantic | Linux | Windows native | WSL2 | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| platform identity | real | real | detected | real |
| state/config paths | real | real | real fixture/acceptance | real |
| filesystem safety | real | real | real fixture/acceptance | real |
| effective resource evidence | real | host/client only | WSL2/runtime | runtime VM aware |
| trust operations | real | capability/backend | split host/WSL | Keychain/capability |
| browser handoff | real | real | explicit boundary | real |
| secure ephemeral material | real | real | real | real |
| runtime discovery | Docker/Podman | classified | real when available | classified |
| full runtime E2E | Docker/Podman | evidence required | evidence required | evidence required |

Refine the table from implementation evidence.

## CI design

### Linux

Reuse existing static/source, Docker and rootless Podman gates.

### Windows

Add a native Windows hosted-runner gate for build/unit/contract conformance and platform-specific tests.

### macOS

Add hosted-runner gates for Darwin build/unit/contract conformance, with ARM64 and Intel where available/appropriate.

### WSL2

Do not fake WSL2 with cross-compilation or environment variables.

If a reliable hosted WSL2 path is unavailable, document a dedicated/self-hosted acceptance lane and keep support status below TESTED until it passes.

## Architecture guard

Add/update source guard rules so generic/core packages do not gain new direct:

- `runtime.GOOS` policy branching;
- `/proc` dependencies;
- Linux trust commands;
- Windows/macOS system commands;
- platform-specific path constants;

except in approved platform adapters or explicitly justified runtime-provider implementation directories.

## Support levels

Integrate with the existing platform-support documentation and require evidence for status transitions.

Suggested semantics:

- **SUPPORTED** — full required acceptance for the claimed use case;
- **TESTED** — real platform execution for defined subset;
- **PORTABILITY-VERIFIED** — native contract/build/conformance but no full runtime lifecycle proof;
- **EXPERIMENTAL** — opt-in/incomplete;
- **UNSUPPORTED** — explicit fail-closed boundary.

## No-dead-end requirement

Platform failures must tell the user:

```text
what capability is unavailable
why on this platform/topology
what safe next action exists
```

Examples:

- run inside WSL2;
- start/configure Docker Desktop;
- allocate more VM memory;
- install/export trust manually;
- choose a supported runtime;
- use a remote Target/Node Connector instead.

## Acceptance

- [ ] one shared conformance suite;
- [ ] Linux CI remains authoritative for Linux support;
- [ ] Windows native CI exists;
- [ ] macOS native CI exists;
- [ ] WSL2 real-evidence requirement is explicit;
- [ ] architecture guard blocks new host leakage;
- [ ] docs/support matrix is generated or audited against CI evidence where practical;
- [ ] no platform is promoted beyond its evidence;
- [ ] failures are typed and actionable;
- [ ] release gates can select the relevant platform proofs without multiplying full pre-release runs unnecessarily.


## Release assignment (2026-10-10)
This platform item now belongs to **v0.4.29 #876**, not the old v0.4.25 plan. Two sessions: Host/Linux/WSL2 (#819–#821) and Darwin/macOS + qualification (#822–#823); final audit #817. Use the v0.4.25 #872 contract baseline; D1/D2 extensions require explicit #819/#876 review before implementation. Final release-wide acceptance #174 is v0.4.31. Real runtime evidence is required.

---

## macOS supplement (2026-10-14)

Authoritative target and decisions D1–D5: #876. v0.4.29 macOS covers Dev Local on both Docker Desktop and Podman Machine; automatic Keychain trust and macOS Dev Remote belong to #886, signing/notarization to #885. WSL2 Dev Local/Remote acceptance in #821 is unchanged. Manual macOS host trust and runtime/workload TLS remain in scope.

### macOS evidence lanes (four separate lanes, each proving only what it can)

| Lane | Runner | Proves | Does not prove |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| darwin compile | `ubuntu-latest` (`GOOS=darwin` build/vet), from #882 | darwin compiles | anything at runtime |
| darwin native | hosted `macos-latest` (arm64); Intel hosted runner only while available | native build, unit tests, host-adapter conformance, PTY, paths, ephemeral secrets, read-only trust status, artifact/update selection | container runtime (hosted Apple Silicon runners have no nested virtualization) |
| linux/arm64 stack | hosted `ubuntu-24.04-arm` | the BaseHarbor container stack on linux/arm64 (Docker + rootless Podman), currently "runtime unproven" in `docs/reference/platform-support.md` | macOS host behavior |
| macOS runtime | self-hosted Apple Silicon Mac (#884) | real Docker Desktop and Podman Machine Dev Local journeys, VM capacity, stopped-VM/unshared-path/low-memory negatives, cleanup | Intel macOS, Dev Remote (#886) |

### Workflow surface

`scripts/ci-workflow-policy.sh` enforces a fixed workflow list. Prefer adding the darwin-native and linux/arm64 lanes as jobs in existing workflows (`ci.yml`, `targeted-integration.yml`, `pre-release-runtime-suite.yml`). Change the policy list only if a dedicated self-hosted workflow is required by #884's hardening (trusted triggers only, no fork PRs).

### Support-level transitions for macOS

- `darwin/arm64 + Docker Desktop` and `darwin/arm64 + Podman Machine`: UNSUPPORTED → TESTED after the self-hosted journey passes on an exact SHA; SUPPORTED only after release-candidate qualification and the independent Dev Local walkthrough.
- `darwin/amd64`: at most PORTABILITY-VERIFIED unless real Intel runtime evidence exists.
- Colima, OrbStack, Rancher Desktop: UNSUPPORTED until they have their own evidence.
- Dev Remote on macOS: UNSUPPORTED until #886.

### Added acceptance

- [ ] All four macOS lanes exist and feed the evidence receipts with the runner/environment inventory.
- [ ] The EN/DE support matrix lists each macOS combination with its exact evidence link or UNVERIFIED.
- [ ] Release gates select the macOS runtime lane only when darwin-relevant sources changed, consistent with the existing targeted-gate selection.

- [ ] D1 negatives cover spoofed context names, endpoint/machine mismatch, privilege/isolation distinction and unsafe host file/socket sharing.
- [ ] D2 negatives cover VM OS/daemon overhead, incomplete container stats, stale/unknown capacity and conflicting limits; partial estimates alone never justify SAFE.
- [ ] Independent macOS Dev Local and genuine WSL2 Dev Local/Remote public-documentation walkthroughs are recorded; no cross-build substitutes.
